issue.title: Failed to dedupe: Encrypted drive 'DriveCacheCrypt:': can't merge directories

repository.name: rclone
repository.description: "rsync for cloud storage" - Google Drive, S3, Dropbox, Backblaze B2, One Drive, Swift, Hubic, Wasabi, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob, Azure Files, Yandex Files

issue.body:
#### What is the problem you are having with rclone?
When trying to dedupe a Google Drive remote that uses Crypt on top of Cache an error message is received.

#### What is your rclone version (output from `rclone version`)
```
rclone v1.52.0
- os/arch: linux/amd64
- go version: go1.14.3
```


#### Which OS you are using and how many bits (eg Windows 7, 64 bit)
Linux Debian 10.x


####  Which cloud storage system are you using? (eg Google Drive)
Google Drive


#### The command you were trying to run (eg `rclone copy /tmp remote:tmp`)
 ```rclone dedupe --dry-run DriveCacheCrypt:```


#### A log from the command with the `-vv` flag (eg output from `rclone -vv copy /tmp remote:tmp`)
```
2020/06/08 17:01:13 Failed to dedupe: Encrypted drive 'DriveCacheCrypt:': can't merge directories
```

body:
I think this is a bug in the logging...

According to the docs

> --dedupe-mode skip - removes identical files then skips anything left.

And I think rclone **is** doing that. The files in questions are different because they have different MD5 sums so rclone didn't delete them.

However it did print

> 2020/06/08 19:26:07 NOTICE: Path/To/File: Found 2 duplicates - deleting identical copies

Which is a very misleading log!

What it actually means according to the code is

- Rclone found 2 files with duplicate file names
- It is now going to see if there are any identical files
- and **if** there are any it will remove them

However I think we've all been reading the log as meaning

- Rclone found 2 files which are identical and will delete them

If rclone does find identical files it will print this log

>Deleting %d/%d identical duplicates (%v %q)

But as @animosity22 pointed out,, duplicate files on crypt don't have the same md5sum (because of the encryption is different each time).

I think we can fix the confusion if I make the first log say

> 2020/06/08 19:26:07 NOTICE: Path/To/File: Found 2 files with duplicate names

And add an addition log when using "skip" (there are no logs for it at the moment) saying

> 2020/06/08 19:26:07 NOTICE: Path/To/File: Skipping deletion of 2 files with duplicate names

Would that work?

Ok, that makes sense to me.

So it basically fails because it is on a crypt and it can't find the md5sum to say they are name if I'm getting that.
